text: The 'argument from illusion' (e.g., the straight stick that looks bent in water) supports sense-data theory by claiming that:
choices: Physical objects change their real shape when placed in water
Since what we are directly aware of has a property (bentness) the physical object lacks, the immediate object of awareness must be a mind-dependent sense-datum
Perception is direct and unmediated even in cases of illusion
explanation: The argument runs: in illusion what we are directly aware of has a property (bentness) the physical stick lacks, so the immediate object must be a mind-dependent sense-datum - and by generalization this holds even in veridical cases. Option 0 misdescribes the physics, option 2 denies that illusions occur, and option 3 is the direct-realist conclusion the argument opposes.
